title: Repository bootstrapping: a new product's repository created from the PRD in the browser
description:
Filed by architect-16a01670 from parent task-e7a3d643bde34da7b27495dbda745739 (epic breakdown, human-directed 2026-09-04; owner chose Stage 1 + Stage 2 scope).

VISION Stage 2 'repository bootstrapping' and the product profile 'support exceptionally well: new repository creation'. Re-measured 2026-09-04: a project must already be an initialized directory (`moe init <dir>` / manager Create writes moe.config.json) and `project.bind_repository` binds an EXISTING git repository; there is no scaffold generator and no GitHub repository creation path (`grep -rc "repo create" apps/ tools/` = 0).

FEATURE: 'New product from PRD' in the browser: directory (new or empty), PRD file, product name, optional GitHub owner/visibility. The daemon runs `repository.bootstrap` (operator-only): `git init`; writes the CONTROLLED-PROFILE scaffold (TypeScript; React + Vite web; Node API; PostgreSQL via docker-compose; vitest; Playwright; pnpm workspace; GitHub Actions CI running `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test`; `.env.example`; README with the product name); first commit 'chore: scaffold by Moe'; optional `gh repo create <owner>/<name> --<visibility> --source . --push`; then binds it as the project repository (`project.bind_repository`) and registers it in the manager catalog; receipt `moe-bootstrap-receipt/1` {dir, sha, remoteUrl|null, BOOTSTRAPPED|REFUSED(code)}. The scaffold generator is deterministic and pinned by a profile version constant (golden tree) so every product starts identical. The goal is then created with the PRD (`goal.create_with_source`) and the existing lane continues.

Refusals: BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY, BOOTSTRAP_GIT_UNAVAILABLE, BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE (GitHub is optional - a local-only bootstrap still succeeds and says so), BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE_VERSION_UNKNOWN.
definitionOfDone: `repository.bootstrap` published operator-only, MCP-excluded, with the full roster backfill and bidirectional roster tests; BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY, BOOTSTRAP_GIT_UNAVAILABLE, BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE, BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE_VERSION_UNKNOWN asserted with code + layer.

Scaffold generator golden test pins the exact file tree plus the package.json, compose and CI workflow bytes under a profile version constant; the generated app passes `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm build` in a test that actually runs it (the child run's count lines quoted).

Browser: 'New product from PRD' form -> directory created, first commit exists (`git log --oneline` = 1 line), repository bound, project in the manager catalog, PRD goal created - Playwright journey against a REAL daemon; count line quoted.

GitHub creation tested offline through a port asserting the `gh` argv; the live drive creates a throwaway repository under the owner's account (URL + receipt in a row comment) and refuses cleanly with `gh` absent (BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE while the local bootstrap still succeeds).

Runbook + README updated ('new repository creation' listed as running); gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: REJECTED, planning this as one row: a deterministic scaffold generator with a golden tree AND a real build of the generated app, a new operator-only command doing git init plus an optional GitHub creation plus a binding plus a receipt, a browser form, a Playwright journey, a live GitHub drive and a docs sweep — far past the 12-step/10-file thresholds, so task rail 1 mandates the SPIDR split. REJECTED, folding the scaffold into the command row: the generator is the highest-risk piece and its 'the generated app actually builds' clause is slow and disk-heavy; isolating it means that cost is paid once, in a row with no dependencies, and the command row can assume a working tree. REJECTED, making GitHub creation mandatory: `gh` is absent on most machines, and a bootstrap that fails wholesale without it would make the feature unusable — child 2 treats a local-only bootstrap as a SUCCESS with remoteUrl null. REJECTED, a stored GitHub token: same decision as Gate 3 (task-f961dc89) — secret handling is out of scope under the FEATURES ONLY rail, so `gh` CLI only.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb. THE GAP IS REAL: `grep -rn 'repository\.bootstrap|CONTROLLED_PROFILE|scaffold' --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` finds only `moe init`, which scaffolds a STORE, an operator credential and moe.config.json (cli/moe-cli-main.ts:16,58) — not a product; and `grep -rc 'repo create' apps/ tools/` = 0, so no GitHub creation path exists. `project.bind_repository` already binds an EXISTING repository and is what child 2 reuses rather than writing a second binding. `goal.create_with_source` already creates a goal from a PRD, so child 3's form ends by calling something that exists. THE PROFILE the scaffold must emit (VISION 'one controlled product profile first'): TypeScript, React + Vite web, Node API, PostgreSQL via docker-compose, vitest, Playwright, pnpm workspace, GitHub Actions CI running `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test`, `.env.example`, README with the product name. A CROSS-EPIC DEPENDENCY WORTH CHECKING AT ROLL-UP: the containerized-deployment, migrations and monitoring rows all assume a compose file with postgres and a `pnpm db:migrate` script — if the scaffold does not emit what they assume, they each discover it separately, so step 4(d) checks it here.
planningNotes.risks: BIGGEST RISK — destroying an operator's existing work. `repository.bootstrap` writes a whole tree at a path the operator types, and BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY is the only thing between it and someone's directory. Child 2 asserts the one-file case; step 4(a) pushes on the boundaries it did not name (a dotfile-only directory, a path that is a file, a trailing separator, a symlink). SECOND — a scaffold that was never built. A golden file-tree test passes on a tree that cannot install; child 1's DoD forces a real install/typecheck/test/build of the generated app, and step 2 requires quoting that CHILD run's output — conflating it with moe-next's own suite is how a broken scaffold would be reported green. THIRD — partial bootstrap states: `gh` failing after the commit, or `gh repo create --push` creating the repository but failing the push; the receipt must be honest about each, and step 4(b) asks. FOURTH — non-determinism creeping in through host paths, timestamps or tool versions baked into generated files, which would only show up when two products are compared much later. FIFTH — the browser-only claim being voided by a scratchpad helper somewhere in the journey; step 5(b) requires stating that none was used. SIXTH — the scaffold not matching what the deployment, migration and monitoring rows assume, which would surface as three separate mid-flight discoveries; step 4(d) checks it once here.
